about: Every word both apps put on screen. One entry per key: `text`, or a `count` argument and one template per CLDR plural category (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). `{name}` is a placeholder. `surface` is where it is drawn, and test/data/surfaces.json holds each surface's length budget. `apps` says which app uses it; `example` is the arguments the fixture and the budget render it with. Design: LANGUAGE.md §2.

readout.phase.coolingIce.text: Leave them in the ice bath

readout.sub.coldAssumes.note: Under the time while idle on a cold start: the time to boil, whether guessed or remembered, with no certainty of its own; the certainty line below speaks for both (DECISIONS.md 99). Its (i) shows only when it is remembered.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.info.note: The name of the (i) beside readout.sub.coldAssumes.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.note: What "based on history" means. True to estimateTimeToBoil and rememberBoil in src/core/policy.ts: keyed by water volume, each boil blended 50/50, else the nearest volume scaled by litres.
readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.text: How long water takes on average until it’s boiling hard all over, refined by your past timings. Press Full rolling boil today and I’ll correct the time while the eggs cook.

readout.sub.standing.text: measure out {water} of water, and keep the lid on

readout.sub.hot.text: from eggs in to eggs out

readout.sub.coolingPeak.note: E4: the countdown ends when the model has the yolk’s centre at its hottest.
readout.sub.coolingPeak.text: until the middle of the yolk stops warming

readout.sub.coolingProbe.note: E4: as coolingPeak, for a cook who said they have a probe thermometer.
readout.sub.coolingProbe.text: have the probe ready for when the middle of the yolk stops warming

readout.alarm.denied.text: notifications are off, so keep the app open

readout.alarm.failed.text: I couldn’t set the alarm, so keep the app open

readout.alarm.set.note: {time} is a time of day with seconds, in the locale’s own clock.

readout.restored.text: After the reload the times are still right, but I can’t sound the alarm, so watch the clock.

refusal.whiteNeverSets.text: With the heat off, the water cools before the white sets. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.harderThanPan.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.harderThanPan.text: With the heat off, this much water ({water}) cools too soon to make the yolk any firmer. Firmest possible: {limit}. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.counter.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.counter.text: In the air the yolk keeps cooking after the egg comes out. Softest possible: {limit}. For a softer yolk, cool the eggs in an ice bath.

refusal.tap.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.tap.text: Cold running water doesn’t cool the egg fast enough to stop the yolk cooking. Softest possible: {limit}. For a slightly softer yolk, use an ice bath.

refusal.ice.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.ice.text: Any shorter and the white is still raw. Softest possible for this egg: {limit}.

warn.wildGuess.note: While idle, in place of a refusal, when the slider rests on a level the pan can deliver but that is a wild guess so far, softer or firmer than every level that is not: the dotted part of the track (reach.ts, lowOddsAt). {doneness} is the doneness word on screen, which stands alone before the colon. The certainty draft; it was warn.lowOdds, 3 times in 10.

action.hint.cold.text: eggs in the pan, lid on, then press Start heating

action.hint.hotStanding.text: eggs into boiling water, then heat off, lid on

action.hint.hotBoiling.text: eggs into boiling water, and keep it boiling hard for all {time}

action.hint.heating.text: wait for the whole surface to roll

action.hint.heating.info.note: The name of the (i) beside action.hint.heating.
action.hint.heating.info.text: When to press Full rolling boil

action.hint.heating.more.text: Press Full rolling boil when the whole surface starts bubbling hard and stirring doesn’t calm it. I time the rest of the cooking from your input here, so get this right!

action.hint.heatingStanding.text: wait for the whole surface to roll, then heat off, lid on

action.hint.cookingStanding.text: lid on until the eggs come out

action.hint.cookingBoiling.text: at {boiling} until the eggs come out

action.hint.pull.text: cooling starts on its own in {seconds} s

ask.stillIn.note: In place of the phase label, when the alarm's grace ran out (so I assumed the eggs came out) and a correction since would cook them longer: I ask, since either could be true (DECISIONS.md 98).
ask.stillIn.text: Are the eggs still in the water?

ask.stillIn.yes.note: The answer to ask.stillIn that the eggs are still in: I time them again as corrected.

ask.stillIn.no.note: The answer to ask.stillIn that the eggs came out when the alarm ended.

readout.sub.stillIn.note: Under the time while ask.stillIn is asked: the time is how long since the eggs were due out.

spoken.stillIn.note: What a screen reader hears while ask.stillIn is asked. {time} is spoken, as spoken.minutesSeconds.
spoken.stillIn.text: Are the eggs still in the water? They were due out {time} ago.

spoken.minutesSeconds.note: {minutes} is spoken.minutes and {seconds} is spoken.seconds, each already in the form its number needs.

spoken.probe.text: Now push the probe to the middle of the egg.

spoken.sousVide.note: {when} is the start phrase, lower-cased by the app.

example.subline: at 8:47 AM — 22 h 43 min at 136 °F, to eat now

controls.doneness.value.note: The doneness slider’s value to a screen reader: the doneness word and the peak yolk it asks for. The two are not drawn together: the word is on the ticks, and the temperature is controls.doneness.peak, at the end of the slider’s heading.

controls.doneness.valueBath.note: As controls.doneness.value, in sous-vide, where there is no peak: the water’s temperature.

controls.doneness.peak.note: At the end of the doneness slider’s heading, across from controls.doneness: the peak yolk temperature the level asks for.

controls.doneness.bath.note: As controls.doneness.peak, in sous-vide, where there is no peak: the water’s temperature.

controls.egg.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside the egg in the setup sentence (UI.md section 4).
controls.egg.more.text: A bigger egg takes longer, because the heat has further to go. Eggs vary a lot, so weigh one if you can.

controls.measure.legend.text: Or fill in any one measurement

controls.measure.hint.text: Weighing is the most accurate. Otherwise, wrap a strip of paper around the fattest part and measure the strip.

controls.eggFrom.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Egg from (UI.md section 4).
controls.eggFrom.more.text: Eggs from the fridge give the most reliable times, because a fridge temperature is consistent.

controls.eggFrom.hint.text: I assume {fridge} for a fridge and {room} for a room. Pick Custom if yours differ.

controls.start.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Start (UI.md section 4). Replaces controls.start.hint.
controls.start.more.text: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water that’s boiling hard. They peel more easily this way. Cold water: put the eggs in a cold pan, turn the heat on, and press Full rolling boil when the water rolls. This is quicker overall. Sous-vide: I’ll tell you how long the eggs need in the water.

controls.startedAt.note: In the start's panel while a cook runs: the time of day the eggs went in, with a − and a + that move it a minute at a time.

controls.startedAt.latestNow.note: Under controls.startedAt when + has gone as far as it can: the eggs cannot have gone in later than now.
controls.startedAt.latestNow.text: I can’t move it later than now.

controls.startedAt.latestBoil.note: Under controls.startedAt when + has gone as far as it can: no later than the press of Full rolling boil, which a cold start would read as before the eggs went in. {time} is that press's time of day.
controls.startedAt.latestBoil.text: I can’t move it later than {time}, when you pressed Full rolling boil.

controls.startedAt.latestPull.note: Under controls.startedAt when + has gone as far as it can: no later than when the eggs were due out. {time} is that time of day.
controls.startedAt.latestPull.text: I can’t move it later than {time}, when the eggs were due out.

controls.startedAt.earliest.note: Under controls.startedAt when − has gone as far as it can: two hours before Start was pressed, the most the app takes for water to boil. {time} is that time of day.
controls.startedAt.earliest.text: I can’t move it earlier than {time}, two hours before I started timing.

controls.afterTheBoil.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Once it’s boiling (UI.md section 4), in both apps.
controls.afterTheBoil.more.text: Keep boiling: keep the water boiling hard until the eggs come out. The amount of water hardly matters. Heat off, lid on: once the eggs are in, turn the heat off and the hot water continues to cook the eggs. This saves energy, but the time depends on how much water there is, so measure it. With too little water the eggs won’t cook through.

controls.cooling.note: The heading of the cooling choice, opened from the setup sentence; its choices are controls.cooling.*.

controls.cooling.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Cooling (UI.md section 4).
controls.cooling.more.text: The yolk keeps cooking for a few minutes after the eggs come out of the water. An ice bath stops it fastest, so it allows the softest yolks, and cold running water is nearly as good. In the air the egg cools so slowly that the softest yolks aren’t possible.

controls.water.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Water (UI.md section 4).
controls.water.more.text: How much water is in the pan, not counting the eggs. Mostly matters if you turn off the heat after boiling, and a little bit to estimate boiling time.

controls.eggsInPan.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Eggs in the pan (UI.md section 4).
controls.eggsInPan.more.text: The more cold eggs you put in, the more they cool the water, so they take longer to cook. On a cold-water start I don’t need this, because the time-to-boiling already accounts for it.

controls.altitude.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Altitude (UI.md section 4).
controls.altitude.more.text: The higher you are, the lower the temperature water boils at, so eggs take longer to cook, especially in the mountains.

controls.settings.note: The page (web) or group (iOS) of settings that belong to the kitchen rather than the egg: units, altitude, water, eggs in the pan, what to do once it’s boiling, the probe, and what I’ve learned (UI.md).

help.link.note: Opens the Help page, from the top of the egg and Settings pages.

help.motto.note: The motto, a short line under the Help page’s title. Keep it short and balanced: what to time, and what not.

help.how.p1.text: I calculate how heat travels through an egg and how far the yolk and white set, and pick the time that gives you the yolk you asked for.

help.how.aside.note: A technical aside under the gist above, drawn smaller. [label](https://…) becomes a link; keep the URLs as they are.
help.how.aside.text: I model [heat conduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation) through a sphere the size of your egg, and protein setting as a dose of heat over time, with the [Arrhenius equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhenius_equation). Every constant and its source is in the [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#2-the-physical-model).

help.how.p2.text: The cooling time also counts as cooking time, since the egg is still warm inside.

help.how.aside2.note: A technical aside under the gist above, drawn smaller. [label](https://…) becomes a link; keep the URLs as they are.
help.how.aside2.text: Still air takes heat out so slowly that the yolk ends up within a fraction of a degree of where it would if the egg never cooled at all. [README §5](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#5-carryover-the-cooling-step-is-part-of-the-recipe).

help.learn.p1.text: Your answers tell me how you like your yolk and how your eggs cook. When you press Full rolling boil, I learn how long your water takes to boil. A probe reading, if you take one, tells me how fast heat gets into your eggs. You don’t have to answer anything.

help.learn.aside.note: A technical aside under the gist above, drawn smaller. [label](https://…) becomes a link; keep the URLs as they are.
help.learn.aside.text: I use [sequential Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_filter) to learn about your eggs and your taste, with an [ordered probit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_probit) for the yolk you got, runny to hard, and the white next to it. I keep a record of every egg, so when I’m updated, I relearn from all of them. [The design](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer/blob/main/INFERENCE.md).

help.reliable.intro.text: The biggest help is telling me how each egg came out. After that, it depends on how you cook.

help.reliable.forYou.note: Above the advice.* lines for the setup on screen (reach.ts, protocolAdvice): shown only when the word asked is a wild guess at the time on screen and a change the model prices raises its chance by ADVICE_GAIN (0.05) or more.

help.reliable.every.text: Weigh the egg if you can, because eggs vary a lot. Eggs straight from the fridge have a more consistent temperature, which helps.

help.reliable.hot.text: This is the easiest way to get right. Keep the water boiling hard the whole time.

help.reliable.cold.text: Wait until the whole surface is rolling before you press Full rolling boil. The first bubbles are too soon. Pressing it lets me correct the time while the eggs cook.

help.reliable.heatOff.text: The water does all the cooking, so measure it, and use plenty. With too little, the white never sets.

help.reliable.cooling.text: An ice bath gives the most reliable result, and cold running water is nearly as good. Air cooling is mediocre.

help.odds.p1.note: Help's gist of how sure I am: the three words on the certainty line below the time, what each means, and what pressing it shows (the certainty draft).
help.odds.p1.text: I can’t promise every egg. Below the time display I say how sure I am of it. Very certain means that 9 times in 10 you’ll get the yolk you asked for. A ballpark figure means that 9 times in 10 you’ll get that yolk or the one next to it on the slider. Anything less sure is a wild guess. Press the words to see which yolks you’re likely to get, and a likely range for the right time.

help.odds.aside.note: A technical aside under the gist above, drawn smaller. [label](https://…) becomes a link; keep the URLs as they are.
help.odds.aside.text: Nine eggs out of ten will cook to a target inside the bracket. I try to err on the side of cooking too long, since a runny white is usually worse than an overfirm yolk. The stronger the shading on the slider, the more often you get the yolk you asked for. Dots mark the yolks that are still a wild guess.

help.unsure.counter.text: I’m least sure about cooling in the air, because I couldn’t find any published measurements of how fast an egg cools in still air.

help.unsure.heatOff.text: With the heat off, I assume an ordinary pan with its lid on. A heavy pot or a loose lid will change the time.

help.unsure.white.text: When you say a white was runny, I can’t tell whether it set late or whether you call a tender white runny.

help.unsure.sousVide.text: Below {floor}, a sous-vide white stays liquid and moves around inside the shell. I don’t account for that, so my times are unreliable there. At those temperatures I estimate the white takes hours or even days to set, if it sets at all.

help.sources.intro.text: These are the main sources for my numbers. The [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#10-references) lists them all, with what I took from each.

help.privacy.note: The last thing on the Help page: a link to the privacy page (privacy/index.html, served at /privacy), which is plain English outside the catalogue (LANGUAGE.md section 2). Translate the word only.

help.credit.note: The last line of the Help page, under the privacy link: who made the app. [label](https://…) becomes a link; keep the name and the URL as they are.

nav.back.note: Leaves the Settings or Help page for the page it was opened from.

learned.title.note: The heading over learned.* on the Settings page.

more.about.note: The name of an (i) button to a screen reader. {label} is the control’s own label, as it is shown; a language that must decline it can rewrite around it, e.g. with a colon.

controls.less.note: The name of the − button beside a number, to a screen reader: it takes the number down one step, and held down, keeps going. {label} is the number’s own label, as it is shown; it stands alone after the colon, so it need not be declined.

controls.more.note: As controls.less, for the + button, which takes the number up.

more.expanded.note: VoiceOver’s value for an (i) while what it opens is showing. The web says it with aria-expanded.

more.collapsed.note: VoiceOver’s value for an (i) while what it opens is put away.

setup.sentence.note: The setup as one sentence; each placeholder is a setup.* fragment drawn as a button that opens that choice. Reorder freely. Each fragment carries its own preposition and article, so in English this template is only punctuation; if your language needs the fragments in a particular case, write them in that case.

setup.sentenceSousVide.note: As setup.sentence, for sous-vide, where the egg comes from and how it cools change nothing.

setup.egg.note: Opens the sentence. {mass} is a size class’s mass or a measured egg’s, with its unit. Plural, so English needs no article before a number ("a 68 g", "an 80 g").

setup.start.cold.text: into cold water, brought to the boil

setup.start.coldStanding.note: A cold start with the heat off at the boil (the Settings page’s setting).
setup.start.coldStanding.text: into cold water, brought to the boil, heat off and lid on

setup.start.hotStanding.note: A boiling-water start with the heat off (the Settings page’s setting).
setup.start.hotStanding.text: into boiling water, heat off and lid on

setup.cooling.counter.text: then left to cool in the air

setup.clause.note: The name of a clause of the setup sentence to a screen reader. {label} is the choice’s heading, {value} the option chosen, both as shown.

setup.close.note: Closes a choice opened from the setup sentence.

idle.welcome.note: Under the setup sentence before any egg or boil has been learned from, when there is no refusal or advice to show.
idle.welcome.text: I start with times for a typical egg. As you tell me how each egg turns out, I adjust them to your eggs and your taste.

controls.units.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Units (UI.md section 4).
controls.units.more.text: I start with what’s usual where your browser says you are.

controls.units.more.ios.note: controls.units.more on a phone: the web’s says where your browser says you are.
controls.units.more.ios.text: I start with what’s usual where your phone says you are.

controls.thermometer.note: The heading of the probe setting on the Settings page; its checkbox says controls.thermometer.ask.

controls.thermometer.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Probe thermometer (UI.md section 4). Says what controls.probe.hint says, and why.
controls.thermometer.more.text: When the cooling countdown ends, the middle of the yolk is at its hottest, and I’ll ask you for a reading. Push the tip right into the middle and tell me the highest number you see. Anywhere else, or any later, will read too low. The reading tells me how fast heat gets into your eggs. If you cool the eggs in the air there’s no countdown, so I won’t ask.

certainty.veryCertain.note: Below the time display, in place of the direction: how sure I am of the time on screen, when 9 times in 10 the yolk is the word asked (certainty.ts, certaintyAt). The cook presses it to open the interval and the time range in place under it.

certainty.ballpark.note: As certainty.veryCertain, when 9 times in 10 the yolk is the word asked or the one either side of it on the slider.

certainty.wildGuess.note: As certainty.veryCertain, when the yolk is less sure than a ballpark figure: a fresh install at runny to jammy.

certainty.interval.note: First in what pressing the certainty line opens: the fewest neighbouring doneness words that hold 9 eggs in 10 at the time on screen. {hits} in {of} is 9 in 10; {from} and {to} are the softest and firmest doneness words, standing alone after the colon.

certainty.interval.one.note: As certainty.interval, when one doneness word holds 9 eggs in 10.

certainty.mostLikely.note: The likeliest doneness word at the time on screen. Under the certainty line, unpressed, only when it is not the word asked; always in what pressing it opens. {word} stands alone after the colon.

certainty.time.note: Third in what pressing the certainty line opens, while idle: the likely time range, the right cook time's 90% interval for the level asked (certainty.ts, likelyTimeRange; the owner's to confirm, SHIP-0.5.md). {low} and {high} are cook times, m:ss, as the time display shows them.
certainty.time.text: I think the right time is between {low} and {high}.

certainty.timeOut.note: certainty.time once the eggs are cooking, when the time display counts down: the same range as when to take them out (wording.ts, timeRangeWords). {low} and {high} are times of day.
certainty.timeOut.text: I think the right time to take the eggs out is between {low} and {high}.

certainty.help.note: Last in what pressing the certainty line opens, while idle: a link to Help at help.odds, where what the direction's (i) used to say now is.
certainty.help.text: More about how sure I am

outcome.whiteRunny.note: Under the certainty line, when at least one white in five is answered runny.
outcome.whiteRunny.text: The white might still be runny.

outcome.range.note: The bracket under the doneness slider, to a screen reader: the first and last doneness words of the interval the certainty line states, the fewest neighbouring words that hold 9 eggs in 10 at the time on screen (wording.ts, rangeWords; certainty.interval's {from} and {to}).

outcome.range.one.note: As outcome.range, when one doneness word holds 9 eggs in 10 (certainty.interval.one).

outcome.bracket.note: In Help, under help.odds.p1: what the bracket under the slider is, and how to play safe with it. It was first in the direction's (i) until the certainty draft.
outcome.bracket.text: The bracket below the slider shows the range your yolk will probably fall in. If you’d rather not risk a soft yolk, slide right until the left end of the bracket is somewhere you’d be happy with. If you’d rather not risk a firm one, slide left until the right end is.

outcome.why.note: In Help, after outcome.bracket: why the bracket starts wide. It was second in the direction's (i).
outcome.why.text: At first I don’t know your taste, your eggs or your kitchen, so the bracket starts wide. It narrows with each egg you tell me about.

outcome.learning.note: In Help, after outcome.why: what I learn from, and what speeds it up. It was last in the direction's (i).
outcome.learning.text: To help me learn faster, answer both questions after each egg, and on a cold-water start, tell me when the water is boiling hard all over. If you have a probe thermometer, a single reading helps most.

advice.toggle.note: Shown when the word asked is a wild guess (reach.ts, adviceWanted) and a change the model prices raises its chance by ADVICE_GAIN (0.05) or more (protocolAdvice's surer). On iOS it opens the advice.* lines in place; on the web it is a link to Help, at help.reliable.
advice.toggle.text: How to make this more reliable

advice.fridge.note: Shown when the egg is taken to be at room temperature.
advice.fridge.text: Use eggs straight from the fridge, because I know how cold a fridge is but not how warm your room is.

advice.weigh.note: Shown when the egg is a size from the box.
advice.weigh.text: Weigh the egg, because eggs of the same size on the box can need quite different times.

advice.ice.note: Shown under a wild guess when the eggs rest on the counter and an ice bath would raise the chance of the word asked, at the level on screen, by ADVICE_GAIN (0.05) or more (reach.ts, protocolAdvice).
advice.ice.text: Cool the eggs in an ice bath. In the air it’s hard to say how much more the yolk will cook.

advice.moreWater.note: Shown under a wild guess with the heat off when twice the water would raise the chance of the word asked, at the level on screen, by ADVICE_GAIN (0.05) or more (reach.ts, protocolAdvice).
advice.moreWater.text: Use more water. With the heat off, more water stays hot for longer, so the time is more reliable.

learned.literature.text: I haven’t learned anything yet. Tell me how each egg came out, and on a cold-water start, when the water is boiling hard all over.

learned.pan.text: {water} of water takes about {time} to boil

example.pan: 12.50 qt of water takes about 6:40 to boil, based on history

learned.forget.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Forget (UI.md section 4). iOS says the same with learned.forgetExplain.
learned.forget.more.text: I forget all your measurements and revert to the default “typical” estimates. A wrong answer or two will wash out after a few more eggs, so you only need this for weird problems.

learned.confirm.message.text: I’ll forget all your results and how long your water took to boil, and go back to the times for a typical egg.

learned.export.note: Saves every result this device keeps to a file the cook keeps (DECISIONS.md 81): a download on the web, the share sheet on iOS. Nothing is sent. Offered on an empty log too, which says learned.export.none.

learned.export.none.note: Under Export my results, when it is pressed with no result kept.

learning.badge.note: A small mark on the time while sharing is on (E8, DECISIONS.md 3 and 53): the time may be nudged a few seconds, and this says the app is still learning. Its (i) is learning.badge.more.

learning.badge.more.note: The (i) on the Learning mark: why the time may move, that it can cost a little (DECISIONS.md 61), and how to stop it.
learning.badge.more.text: You’re sharing your results, so I’m still learning from them. Now and then I move the time a few seconds either way, up to ten, to learn what happens just off the time I’d pick. It can leave an egg a little softer or firmer than I’d otherwise aim for. Turn sharing off in Settings and the time stays where I’d put it.

share.title.note: The heading of the Settings section for sharing (E6, INFERENCE.md section 7), with its (i), share.more.

share.toggle.note: The switch that turns sharing on; off until the cook turns it on.

share.what.note: The consent, always on screen beside the switch, never behind an (i): what is sent, that nothing names the cook, and that the time may move (the nudge, DECISIONS.md 3 and 53). It has to stay true: if the app sends more, this says so.
share.what.text: I’ll send your results, including past ones: how each egg was cooked and how you said it came out. No name or place: a random ID made on this device stands in for you. While this is on, I’ll sometimes move a time a few seconds either way, to learn faster.

share.more.note: The (i) beside share.title: why, exactly what goes, and the way back. The water's boiling point is named because it says roughly how high up the cook is.
share.more.text: Results from one kitchen tell me only about that kitchen. Results from many show me how eggs, pots, water and cooling really differ, and the next version of the app starts everyone from what they show. I send each egg’s size, how it was cooked, the water’s boiling point (which says roughly how high up you are), your answers, and what I expected. Moving a time a few seconds teaches me what the usual times can’t, and stays within just right. Turn this off whenever you like, and press Delete shared results to remove every one from the server.

share.none.note: Under the switch, sharing on, before any egg has gone.

share.waiting.note: After share.sent, when eggs are waiting for the network.
share.waiting.one: {eggs} more will go when I can reach the server.
share.waiting.other: {eggs} more will go when I can reach the server.

share.id.note: Over the cook's random id, shown whole and selectable once sharing has been turned on (DECISIONS.md 67), so that it can be quoted in an email asking for deletion. The privacy page calls it the random ID.

share.delete.note: Deletes every egg this device has sent, under every id it has used, after share.confirm.*.

share.confirm.message.text: I’ll ask the server to delete every result this device has sent, and stop sharing. What I’ve learned here stays.

share.deleting.note: While the server has not yet confirmed a deletion; it is asked again at every launch until it does.
share.deleting.text: Deleting. If I can’t reach the server now, I’ll keep asking until it confirms.

share.deleted.text: Deleted: the server has nothing this device sent.

feedback.target.note: Above the yolk question after a cook: what the cook was started for, from what was started, not the slider now, so the answer is graded against it. {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app; {yolk} the peak yolk, with its unit.

feedback.invite.text: Your answers help me fit the times to your taste and your eggs.

feedback.thanks.text: Thanks. I’ll use that next time.

feedback.optional.note: Under the two questions and the probe reading after a cook; when the cook has no probe reading to give (cooled in the air), under the two questions alone.

feedback.white.ask.note: The white the model scores: the innermost, next to the yolk, which sets last (INFERENCE.md section 3). The white next to the shell is nearly always set.
feedback.white.ask.text: And the white next to the yolk?

controls.thermometer.ask.note: The checkbox under the Probe thermometer heading. No pronoun: the app is "I" everywhere, so a control the cook taps never speaks as "I".
controls.thermometer.ask.text: Ask for a reading after each egg

controls.room.note: The room setting, under Probe thermometer on the Settings page and shown only while the probe is on: the kitchen's air, measured with the probe. Optional; an empty field shows the room assumed, greyed.

controls.room.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Room temperature (UI.md section 4). {room} is the room assumed when the field is empty, in the cook's units. The model cools eggs in the air, and water left to stand with the heat off, toward the room, starts a cold pan's water at it, and takes an egg left out to be at it.
controls.room.more.text: Optional. Hold your probe in the air of your kitchen and set what it reads. It matters most for eggs left out at room temperature and eggs cooled in the air. Leave it blank and I’ll assume {room}.

probe.ask.note: Under the yolk and white questions after a cook, over the thermometer reading, which is optional (DECISIONS.md 92). Shown whenever the cook has a moment to probe: the cooling countdown ended at the yolk's peak.
probe.ask.text: Do you have a probe thermometer?

probe.how.note: Under probe.ask. Now, because the countdown has just ended at the yolk's peak, and every later reading is lower: the highest number is the middle, and every mistake reads low (INFERENCE.md section 5).
probe.how.text: Push it into the middle of the yolk now and tell me the highest number you see.

probe.refused.text: That’s not what I’d expect from the middle of this egg, which should read {low} to {high}. Is the tip in the yolk?

sousvide.subline.note: {clock} is a time of day, in the locale’s own clock.
sousvide.subline.text: at {clock}, for {duration} at {bath}, to eat now

sousvide.note.whiteBound.text: white only just set, yolk firmer than you asked

sousvide.note.yolkBound.text: yolk as you asked, white set

sousvide.warn.text: At {bath} the white takes most of a day to set, if it sets at all. My times aren’t reliable below {floor}, so boil the eggs instead.

sousvide.hint.text: nothing to start, and you’re {duration} late

sousvide.start.lastWeekday.note: {weekday} is a weekday name, from weekday.* in this catalogue, in both apps.

controls.language.note: F6: the language picker in Settings (LANGUAGE.md section 6).

controls.language.more.note: F6: what the (i) beside Language opens.
controls.language.more.text: English (1750) is English as Samuel Johnson wrote it. I switch to it when you pick Imperial. Pick English to keep Imperial in today’s English.

language.en.note: F6: a language’s own name, the same in every catalogue, so it can be found from any of them.

controls.alarm.note: Settings: which sound the alarm makes, three to choose from (DECISIONS.md 101).

controls.alarm.more.note: What the (i) beside Alarm sound opens. The two moments are the pull and the end of the cooling; the credit is for the hen’s two recordings, CC0, from freesound.org.
controls.alarm.more.text: What you hear when it’s time to take the eggs out, and when they’ve cooled. Choose one to hear it. The hen’s calls were recorded by Jofae and Rudmer Rotteveel, who share them on Freesound.

controls.alarm.timer.note: The default: a clockwork kitchen timer’s bell.

controls.alarm.hen.note: Two recordings of a hen: her alarm call at the pull, and the cackle she makes after laying when the eggs have cooled.

controls.units.period.note: F6: one line under the Imperial option, in an English UI (LANGUAGE.md section 6: discoverable, reluctantly).
controls.units.period.text: I can also write Imperial units in the English of their day.

app.titlePage.note: F6: heads the egg’s page in the English of 1750 only, after the Dictionary’s own title page. Its 1750 twin, and only that, has the long s; the page gives it an aria-label with every long s an s.
app.titlePage.text: The Actual Egg-Timer: in which the times of boiling are deduced from their causes, and illustrated in their different degrees of hardness.

alarm.pull.bodyIce.note: Also the Lock Screen card’s line at the pull. Names the cooling the cook chose.
alarm.pull.bodyIce.text: Straight into the ice bath, or the yolk keeps cooking.

alarm.pull.bodyTap.note: Also the Lock Screen card’s line at the pull. Names the cooling the cook chose.
alarm.pull.bodyTap.text: Straight under the cold running water, or the yolk keeps cooking.

alarm.pull.bodyCounter.text: Take them out and let them cool in the air.

alarm.cooled.body.text: The yolk has stopped cooking. Your eggs are ready.

alarm.probe.body.text: Push the probe into the middle of the egg and tell me the highest number.

activity.stage.pull.note: No "now": the card’s big text beside it says NOW.

activity.target.note: {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.

activity.summary.note: {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.

activity.note.estimate.text: my guess until Full rolling boil

colophon.lede.text: I work out each time from how heat gets into an egg.

colophon.tail.text: are open for anyone to check.

colophon.version.note: The last line of Settings, under the colophon: which version of the app this is, so that someone writing in can say which. {version} is the number, shown whole in a fixed-width face and selectable, to copy: on the web the release, such as 0.4.0-alpha.1; on iOS the App Store version and, in brackets, the build, such as 0.4.0 (2).

newer.note.note: At the top of every screen, and only when a newer version of the app has run on this device and this older one is open (DECISIONS.md 100). It still times eggs but writes nothing: it keeps no setting, logs and learns from no egg, and sends nothing. Updating is the fix in both apps; on the web a reload brings the newest version.
newer.note.text: A newer edition of this app saved your results. Until you update this one, I’ll time your eggs but won’t save or learn anything.
